title: Burst admission controller: initial service skeleton + Admit API wiring
author: Benji Okafor
description: Summary This PR introduces the initial skeleton for the Burst Admission Controller service, including the public (internal-to-platform) Admit API, request/response models, and basic wiring to the policy engine for deterministic evaluation. This is intentionally scoped to a minimum viable service surface so routing/gateway can start integrating against stable types and error semantics while we iterate on fairness/cooldown and fleet telemetry integration in follow-ups. Motivation Dedicated Burst Capacity requires a single decision point that can (a) determine whether a request can borrow burst capacity given tenant config + global safety rules and (b) return a structured denial reason when it cannot. This PR establishes the service boundaries, API contract, and the first deterministic policy evaluation path (config + static guardrails), without yet depending on live GPU telemetry signals. What’s included - New service: burst-admission-controller (HTTP/gRPC gateway wrapper, standard Redwood service scaffolding, deployment manifests) - Endpoint: POST /v1/burst/admit (internal) - Request model includes tenant_id, region, hardware_class, requested_units, baseline_units, request_id, and optional priority_tier - Response model includes decision (ADMIT | DENY), decision_ttl_ms, denial_reason_code, and redacted debug fields for internal logs - Policy wiring: calls policy-engine with a BurstAdmissionContext, evaluating configured guardrail rules (max_burst_ratio, per-tenant cap, region/hardware allowlist) - Determinism: evaluation is purely config-based in this PR; no time-varying telemetry inputs yet (except for an injected monotonic clock used only for decision TTL) - Basic metrics: request_count, decision_count{admit|deny,reason}, and evaluation_latency_ms - Standardized error mapping: 400 for validation errors, 403 for hard policy denies (DENY), 503 for dependency failures (policy-engine unavailable) - Feature gating: service supports a global flag burst.admission_controller.enabled and per-tenant enablement (read-only lookup stub, to be backed by control plane in ENG-4816) Not included (follow-ups) - Fairness / token buckets / anti-starvation - Cooldown windows - Queue/backpressure mode (this PR is immediate decision only) - Fleet telemetry / pool saturation inputs - Full audit logging and RBAC controls (tracked separately) - Billing/metering hooks Implementation notes - The service uses Redwood’s standard service kit (config loader, auth middleware, tracing). - Request validation is strict to avoid implicit defaults that could become non-deterministic later (e.g., hardware_class is required; baseline_units must be provided by caller until we own baseline lookup). - Denial reason codes are intentionally minimal for now: BURST_DISABLED, TENANT_NOT_ENABLED, REGION_NOT_ALLOWED, HARDWARE_CLASS_NOT_ALLOWED, EXCEEDS_MAX_BURST_RATIO, EXCEEDS_TENANT_CAP, POLICY_ENGINE_ERROR. These will be expanded/standardized in the denial codes PR. Testing - Unit tests for validation, policy-engine request shaping, and error mapping - Golden tests for policy evaluation determinism (same input => same output) - Smoke test harness (local) to hit /v1/burst/admit with sample payloads Rollout plan - Land behind the global feature flag (default disabled). - Deploy service to staging once merged. - Routing integration can begin using the types and endpoint, still gated by its own feature flag until fairness + telemetry are ready. Checklist - [x] API contract + OpenAPI stub published to internal service registry - [x] Metrics emitted and scraped - [x] Tracing spans added around policy evaluation - [x] Basic runbook stub (TODO markers for alerts once SRE defines thresholds) - [x] Load shedding defaults (max in-flight requests) - [ ] Security review for authZ model (tracked in ENG-4870) References - ENG-4810 Implement burst admission controller - ADR (in review): admission control semantics and determinism constraints

review_conversation: Jordan Lee: Can we guarantee determinism if we later add telemetry? I want the contract to explicitly state which inputs can affect a decision. Also, please avoid server-side baseline lookups in this PR—callers should send baseline_units for now so routing has the same view.

Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Kept evaluation purely config-based here; no telemetry reads. Added comments to BurstAdmissionContext about permitted inputs and updated handler to require baseline_units (no fallback lookup).

Mina Haddad: Routing needs a stable response shape for denials. Can we ensure denial_reason_code is always populated on DENY (and empty on ADMIT) and that 4xx vs 5xx is consistent? Also, request_id should be echoed back for tracing.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated response contract: on DENY we always set denial_reason_code; on ADMIT it’s empty. Validation errors return 400 with details; hard policy denies return 200 with decision=DENY (not 403) so routing can treat as expected control flow; only auth failures are 401/403. Also echoed request_id in response headers and logs; can add to body if you prefer.

Ethan Park: +1 to returning 200 for DENY; otherwise we’ll conflate policy denies with transport failures. Please ensure the policy-engine dependency failure maps to 503 and includes a retry-after hint (or at least TTL) so callers can backoff.

Benji Okafor (author): Added 503 mapping for policy-engine errors and decision_ttl_ms on all responses. For 503 we set Retry-After=1s (configurable) and include a reason string in logs only (not in response body).
Keiko Yamamoto: Where will max_burst_ratio live? I don’t want hardcoded constants. Also, add max in-flight to protect the service itself (burst storms).

Benji Okafor (author): max_burst_ratio is expressed as a policy rule and loaded via config; no hardcoded defaults besides safe 'deny unless enabled'. Added max_in_flight=200 with 429 on overload (service-level), separate from burst deny semantics.

Sean Gallagher: Please add a runbook stub and at least one metric that allows us to alert on policy-engine unavailability (e.g., dependency_error_count). Also confirm logs don’t leak tenant config details.

Benji Okafor (author): Added dependency_error_count and a README runbook section with TODOs for alert thresholds. Logs redact tenant config (we log only tenant_id, region, hardware_class, decision, and reason code).
merge_outcome: Merged to main; service deployable behind feature flag (default disabled).
release_notes: Internal: Introduces burst admission controller service skeleton and Admit API contract (gated, no customer-facing change).
